answer: Persistent activity entropy pricing. Each identity pays a per-action fee that decays with idle time since its last verified action, like a pulse that must be kept warm. New identities start on the expensive tundra tier, where each action costs many multiples of a long-lived agent's rate. Freshly created sybils therefore face steep per-operation cost with no fable of cheap entry. Sustaining N identities over time costs far more than one mature identity doing the same work.
